title: Universal fingerprint of topological defect cores
authors: Zi-Qiang Zhao, Nayun Jia, Zhang-Yu Nie, Hua-Bi Zeng, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang
abstract: Topological defects are ubiquitous in physics, arising from condensed matter physics to the early universe. Although there exist many universal scaling laws for correlations between topological defects, such as Porod scaling, the fingerprint of topological defect cores has remained largely unexplored. Here, we discover a universal scaling law in the region $k>1/ξ$, where $ξ$ is the healing length of the topological defects, taking the scaling of the form factor $S_f \propto k^{-(d+p+2)}$, where $d$ is the spatial dimension and $p$ is the defect codimension. We analytically prove that this exponent originates from a universal V-shaped cusp at the defect core and is independent of the underlying system and dynamics. Numerical simulations verify this scaling law in four typical frameworks: the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau and Gross-Pitaevskii equations in the weak-coupling regime, the gauge/gravity duality model in the strong-coupling regime, and the Klein-Gordon equation in the Friedmann-Robertson-Walker background in cosmology. Our work provides a new probe for studying topological defects in systems ranging from superconductors to cosmological phase transitions.
summary: This work establishes a universal scaling law, $S_f \propto k^{-(d+p+2)}$, that characterizes the spatial fingerprint of topological defect cores. By deriving this law analytically and verifying it numerically across diverse systems—from superconductors to cosmological backgrounds—the authors provide a powerful new diagnostic tool for studying defect physics.
main_problem: The paper aims to discover and analytically prove a universal scaling law for the 'fingerprint' of topological defect cores, an aspect previously unexplored despite existing scaling laws for defect correlations.
main_result: A universal scaling law, $S_f \propto k^{-(d+p+2)}$, is discovered for the form factor in the region $k>1/\xi$, which is analytically proven to originate from a universal V-shaped cusp at the defect core.
method: The authors used theoretical derivation involving the form factor decomposition and confirmed the scaling law through extensive numerical simulations across multiple physical models.
model_or_system: The study examines topological defects (kinks, vortices, domain walls) arising from symmetry breaking in various contexts, including condensed matter (Ginzburg-Landau, Gross-Pitaevskii), cosmology (Klein-Gordon in FRW background), and holographic models (gauge/gravity duality).
key_observables: The primary observable is the form factor, $S_f(\mathbf{k})$, and the diagnostic is the scaling exponent $-(d+p+2)$.
important_parameters: Healing length ($\xi$), spatial dimension ($d$), and defect codimension ($p$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on approximating the core shape using a $	anh$ function, and the numerical simulations test various regimes (weak vs. strong coupling).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spatial configurations of various defects (Kink, Vortex) and show the scaling behavior of the form factor $S_f$ for different defect types using the TDGL model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the gap in knowledge regarding defect core fingerprints, deriving the universal scaling law analytically, and then rigorously verifying this scaling law using numerical simulations across four distinct physical frameworks (TDGL, GP, Holographic, FRW).
why_interesting: The universality of the scaling exponent, independent of the specific microscopic dynamics or underlying system, provides a powerful, model-agnostic diagnostic tool for characterizing topological structures in complex many-body systems.
